| `allow-ksm` | boolean |  | Allow memory pages of this guest to be merged via KSM (Kernel Samepage Merging). — default `1` |
| `amd-sev` | string |  | Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) features by AMD CPUs — format `pve-qemu-sev-fmt` |
| `arch` | `x86_64` \| `aarch64` |  | Virtual processor architecture. Defaults to the host architecture. |

| `autostart` | boolean |  | Automatic restart after crash (currently ignored). — default `0` |

| `balloon` | number |  | Amount of target RAM for the VM in MiB. The balloon driver is enabled by default, unless it is explicitly disabled by setting the value to zero. — min 0 |
| `bios` | `seabios` \| `ovmf` |  | Select BIOS implementation. — default `"seabios"` |
| `boot` | string |  | Specify guest boot order. Use the 'order=' sub-property as usage with no key or 'legacy=' is deprecated. — format `pve-qm-boot` |
| `bootdisk` | string |  | Enable booting from specified disk. Deprecated: Use 'boot: order=foo;bar' instead. — format `pve-qm-bootdisk` |
| `cdrom` | string |  | This is an alias for option -ide2 — format `pve-qm-ide` |
| `cicustom` | string |  | cloud-init: Specify custom files to replace the automatically generated ones at start. — format `pve-qm-cicustom` |
| `cipassword` | string |  | cloud-init: Password to assign the user. Using this is generally not recommended. Use ssh keys instead. Also note that older cloud-init versions do not support hashed passwords. |
| `citype` | `configdrive2` \| `nocloud` \| `opennebula` |  | Specifies the cloud-init configuration format. The default depends on the configured operating system type (`ostype`. We use the `nocloud` format for Linux, and `configdrive2` for windows. |
| `ciupgrade` | boolean |  | cloud-init: do an automatic package upgrade after the first boot. — default `1` |
| `ciuser` | string |  | cloud-init: User name to change ssh keys and password for instead of the image's configured default user. |
| `cores` | number |  | The number of cores per socket. — min 1, default `1` |
| `cpu` | string |  | Emulated CPU type. — format `pve-vm-cpu-conf` |
| `cpulimit` | number |  | Limit of CPU usage. — min 0, max 128, default `0` |
| `cpuunits` | number |  | CPU weight for a VM, will be clamped to [1, 10000] in cgroup v2. — min 1, max 262144, default `"cgroup v1: 1024, cgroup v2: 100"` |
| `delete` | string |  | A list of settings you want to delete. — format `pve-configid-list` |
| `description` | string |  | Description for the VM. Shown in the web-interface VM's summary. This is saved as comment inside the configuration file. — ≤ 8192 chars |
| `digest` | string |  | Prevent changes if current configuration file has different SHA1 digest. This can be used to prevent concurrent modifications. — ≤ 40 chars |
| `efidisk0` | string |  | Configure a disk for storing EFI vars. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Note that SIZE_IN_GiB is ignored here and that the default EFI vars are copied to the volume instead. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. |
| `force` | boolean |  | Force physical removal. Without this, we simple remove the disk from the config file and create an additional configuration entry called 'unused[n]', which contains the volume ID. Unlink of unused[n] always cause physical removal. |
| `freeze` | boolean |  | Freeze CPU at startup (use 'c' monitor command to start execution). |
| `hookscript` | string |  | Script that will be executed during various steps in the vms lifetime. — format `pve-volume-id` |
| `hostpci0`…`hostpci15` | string |  | Map host PCI devices into guest. — format `pve-qm-hostpci` |
| `hotplug` | string |  | Selectively enable hotplug features. This is a comma separated list of hotplug features: 'network', 'disk', 'cpu', 'memory', 'usb' and 'cloudinit'. Use '0' to disable hotplug completely. Using '1' as value is an alias for the default `network,disk,usb`. USB hotplugging is possible for guests with machine version &gt;= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows &gt; 7. — format `pve-hotplug-features`, default `"network,disk,usb"` |
| `hugepages` | `any` \| `2` \| `1024` |  | Enables hugepages memory. Sets the size of hugepages in MiB. If the value is set to 'any' then 1 GiB hugepages will be used if possible, otherwise the size will fall back to 2 MiB. |
| `ide0`…`ide3` | string |  | Use volume as IDE hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 3). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. |
| `import-working-storage` | string |  | A file-based storage with 'images' content-type enabled, which is used as an intermediary extraction storage during import. Defaults to the source storage. — format `pve-storage-id` |
| `intel-tdx` | string |  | Trusted Domain Extension (TDX) features by Intel CPUs — format `pve-qemu-tdx-fmt` |
| `ipconfig0`…`ipconfig31` | string |  | cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface. IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified. The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit gateway should be provided. For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires cloud-init 19.4 or newer. If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using dhcp on IPv4. — format `pve-qm-ipconfig` |
| `ivshmem` | string |  | Inter-VM shared memory. Useful for direct communication between VMs, or to the host. |
| `keephugepages` | boolean |  | Use together with hugepages. If enabled, hugepages will not not be deleted after VM shutdown and can be used for subsequent starts. — default `0` |
| `keyboard` | `de` \| `de-ch` \| `da` \| `en-gb` \| `en-us` \| `es` \| `fi` \| `fr` \| … (17 more) |  | Keyboard layout for VNC server. This option is generally not required and is often better handled from within the guest OS. — default `null` |
| `kvm` | boolean |  | Enable/disable KVM hardware virtualization. — default `1` |
| `localtime` | boolean |  | Set the real time clock (RTC) to local time. This is enabled by default if the `ostype` indicates a Microsoft Windows OS. |
| `lock` | `backup` \| `clone` \| `create` \| `migrate` \| `rollback` \| `snapshot` \| `snapshot-delete` \| `suspending` \| … (1 more) |  | Lock/unlock the VM. |
| `machine` | string |  | Specify the QEMU machine. |
| `memory` | string |  | Memory properties. |
| `migrate_downtime` | number |  | Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations. Should the migration not be able to converge in the very end, because too much newly dirtied RAM needs to be transferred, the limit will be increased automatically step-by-step until migration can converge. Will be capped to 2000 seconds (maximum in QEMU). — min 0, default `0.1` |
| `migrate_speed` | number |  | Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit. — min 0, default `0` |
| `name` | string |  | Set a name for the VM. Only used on the configuration web interface. — format `dns-name` |
| `nameserver` | string |  | cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set. — format `address-list` |
| `net0`…`net31` | string |  | Specify network devices. |
| `node` | string | yes | The cluster node name. — format `pve-node` |
| `numa` | boolean |  | Enable/disable NUMA. — default `0` |
| `numa0`…`numa7` | string |  | NUMA topology. |
| `onboot` | boolean |  | Specifies whether a VM will be started during system bootup. — default `0` |
| `ostype` | `other` \| `wxp` \| `w2k` \| `w2k3` \| `w2k8` \| `wvista` \| `win7` \| `win8` \| … (5 more) |  | Specify guest operating system. — default `"other"` |
| `parallel0`…`parallel2` | string |  | Map host parallel devices (n is 0 to 2). |
| `protection` | boolean |  | Sets the protection flag of the VM. This will disable the remove VM and remove disk operations. — default `0` |
| `reboot` | boolean |  | Allow reboot. If set to '0' the VM exit on reboot. — default `1` |
| `revert` | string |  | Revert a pending change. — format `pve-configid-list` |
| `rng0` | string |  | Configure a VirtIO-based Random Number Generator. — format `pve-qm-rng` |
| `sata0`…`sata5` | string |  | Use volume as SATA hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 5). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. |
| `scsi0`…`scsi30` | string |  | Use volume as SCSI hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 30). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. |
| `scsihw` | `lsi` \| `lsi53c810` \| `virtio-scsi-pci` \| `virtio-scsi-single` \| `megasas` \| `pvscsi` |  | SCSI controller model — default `"lsi"` |
| `searchdomain` | string |  | cloud-init: Sets DNS search domains for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set. |
| `serial0`…`serial3` | string |  | Create a serial device inside the VM (n is 0 to 3) |
| `shares` | number |  | Amount of memory shares for auto-ballooning. The larger the number is, the more memory this VM gets. Number is relative to weights of all other running VMs. Using zero disables auto-ballooning. Auto-ballooning is done by pvestatd. — min 0, max 50000, default `1000` |
| `skiplock` | boolean |  | Ignore locks - only root is allowed to use this option. |
| `smbios1` | string |  | Specify SMBIOS type 1 fields. — format `pve-qm-smbios1`, ≤ 512 chars |
| `smp` | number |  | The number of CPUs. Please use option -sockets instead. — min 1, default `1` |
| `sockets` | number |  | The number of CPU sockets. — min 1, default `1` |
| `spice_enhancements` | string |  | Configure additional enhancements for SPICE. |
| `sshkeys` | string |  | cloud-init: Setup public SSH keys (one key per line, OpenSSH format). — format `urlencoded` |
| `startdate` | string |  | Set the initial date of the real time clock. Valid format for date are:'now' or '2006-06-17T16:01:21' or '2006-06-17'. — default `"now"` |
| `startup` | string |  | Startup and shutdown behavior. Order is a non-negative number defining the general startup order. Shutdown in done with reverse ordering. Additionally you can set the 'up' or 'down' delay in seconds, which specifies a delay to wait before the next VM is started or stopped. — format `pve-startup-order` |
| `tablet` | boolean |  | Enable/disable the USB tablet device. — default `1` |
| `tags` | string |  | Tags of the VM. This is only meta information. — format `pve-tag-list` |
| `tdf` | boolean |  | Enable/disable time drift fix. — default `0` |
| `template` | boolean |  | Enable/disable Template. — default `0` |
| `tpmstate0` | string |  | Configure a Disk for storing TPM state. The format is fixed to 'raw'. Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Note that SIZE_IN_GiB is ignored here and 4 MiB will be used instead. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. |
| `unused0`…`unused255` | string |  | Reference to unused volumes. This is used internally, and should not be modified manually. |
| `usb0`…`usb13` | string |  | Configure an USB device (n is 0 to 4, for machine version &gt;= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows &gt; 7, n can be up to 14). |
| `vcpus` | number |  | Number of hotplugged vcpus. — min 1, default `0` |
| `vga` | string |  | Configure the VGA hardware. |
| `virtio0`…`virtio15` | string |  | Use volume as VIRTIO hard disk (n is 0 to 15). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. |
| `virtiofs0`…`virtiofs9` | string |  | Configuration for sharing a directory between host and guest using Virtio-fs. |
| `vmgenid` | string |  | Set VM Generation ID. Use '1' to autogenerate on create or update, pass '0' to disable explicitly. — default `"1 (autogenerated)"` |
| `vmid` | number | yes | The (unique) ID of the VM. — format `pve-vmid`, min 100, max 999999999 |
| `vmstatestorage` | string |  | Default storage for VM state volumes/files. — format `pve-storage-id` |
| `watchdog` | string |  | Create a virtual hardware watchdog device. — format `pve-qm-watchdog` |

| `hotplug` | string |  | Selectively enable hotplug features. This is a comma separated list of hotplug features: 'network', 'disk', 'cpu', 'memory', 'usb' and 'cloudinit'. Use '0' to disable hotplug completely. Using '1' as value is an alias for the default `network,disk,usb`. USB hotplugging is possible for guests with machine version &gt;= 7.1 and ostype l26 or windows &gt; 7. — format `pve-hotplug-features`, default `"network,disk,usb"` |
| `hugepages` | `any` \| `2` \| `1024` |  | Enables hugepages memory. Sets the size of hugepages in MiB. If the value is set to 'any' then 1 GiB hugepages will be used if possible, otherwise the size will fall back to 2 MiB. |
| `ide0`…`ide3` | string |  | Use volume as IDE hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 3). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. |
| `intel-tdx` | string |  | Trusted Domain Extension (TDX) features by Intel CPUs — format `pve-qemu-tdx-fmt` |
| `ipconfig0`…`ipconfig31` | string |  | cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface. IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified. The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit gateway should be provided. For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration. This requires cloud-init 19.4 or newer. If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using dhcp on IPv4. — format `pve-qm-ipconfig` |
| `ivshmem` | string |  | Inter-VM shared memory. Useful for direct communication between VMs, or to the host. |
| `keephugepages` | boolean |  | Use together with hugepages. If enabled, hugepages will not not be deleted after VM shutdown and can be used for subsequent starts. — default `0` |
| `keyboard` | `de` \| `de-ch` \| `da` \| `en-gb` \| `en-us` \| `es` \| `fi` \| `fr` \| … (17 more) |  | Keyboard layout for VNC server. This option is generally not required and is often better handled from within the guest OS. — default `null` |
| `kvm` | boolean |  | Enable/disable KVM hardware virtualization. — default `1` |
| `localtime` | boolean |  | Set the real time clock (RTC) to local time. This is enabled by default if the `ostype` indicates a Microsoft Windows OS. |
| `lock` | `backup` \| `clone` \| `create` \| `migrate` \| `rollback` \| `snapshot` \| `snapshot-delete` \| `suspending` \| … (1 more) |  | Lock/unlock the VM. |
| `machine` | string |  | Specify the QEMU machine. |
| `memory` | string |  | Memory properties. |
| `migrate_downtime` | number |  | Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations. Should the migration not be able to converge in the very end, because too much newly dirtied RAM needs to be transferred, the limit will be increased automatically step-by-step until migration can converge. Will be capped to 2000 seconds (maximum in QEMU). — min 0, default `0.1` |
| `migrate_speed` | number |  | Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit. — min 0, default `0` |

| `numa` | boolean |  | Enable/disable NUMA. — default `0` |

| `onboot` | boolean |  | Specifies whether a VM will be started during system bootup. — default `0` |
| `ostype` | `other` \| `wxp` \| `w2k` \| `w2k3` \| `w2k8` \| `wvista` \| `win7` \| `win8` \| … (5 more) |  | Specify guest operating system. — default `"other"` |

| `reboot` | boolean |  | Allow reboot. If set to '0' the VM exit on reboot. — default `1` |
| `revert` | string |  | Revert a pending change. — format `pve-configid-list` |
| `rng0` | string |  | Configure a VirtIO-based Random Number Generator. — format `pve-qm-rng` |
| `sata0`…`sata5` | string |  | Use volume as SATA hard disk or CD-ROM (n is 0 to 5). Use the special syntax STORAGE_ID:SIZE_IN_GiB to allocate a new volume. Use STORAGE_ID:0 and the 'import-from' parameter to import from an existing volume. |

Create new rule.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | string | yes | Rule action ('ACCEPT', 'DROP', 'REJECT') or security group name. — ≤ 20 chars |
| `comment` | string |  | Descriptive comment. — format `pve-fw-comment-spec` |
| `dest` | string |  | Restrict packet destination address. This can refer to a single IP address, an IP set ('+ipsetname') or an IP alias definition. You can also specify an address range like '20.34.101.207-201.3.9.99', or a list of IP addresses and networks (entries are separated by comma). Please do not mix IPv4 and IPv6 addresses inside such lists. — format `pve-fw-addr-spec`, ≤ 512 chars |
| `digest` | string |  | Prevent changes if current configuration file has a different digest. This can be used to prevent concurrent modifications. — ≤ 64 chars |
| `dport` | string |  | Restrict TCP/UDP destination port. You can use service names or simple numbers (0-65535), as defined in '/etc/services'. Port ranges can be specified with '\d+:\d+', for example '80:85', and you can use comma separated list to match several ports or ranges. — format `pve-fw-dport-spec` |

```ts

```

Migrate virtual machine. Creates a new migration task.

Returns `string`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bwlimit` | number |  | Override I/O bandwidth limit (in KiB/s). — min 0, default `"migrate limit from datacenter or storage config"` |
| `force` | boolean |  | Allow to migrate VMs which use local devices. Only root may use this option. |
| `migration_network` | string |  | CIDR of the (sub) network that is used for migration. — format `CIDR` |
| `migration_type` | `secure` \| `insecure` |  | Migration traffic is encrypted using an SSH tunnel by default. On secure, completely private networks this can be disabled to increase performance. |
| `node` | string | yes | The cluster node name. — format `pve-node` |
| `online` | boolean |  | Use online/live migration if VM is running. Ignored if VM is stopped. |
| `target` | string | yes | Target node. — format `pve-node` |
| `targetstorage` | string |  | Mapping from source to target storages. Providing only a single storage ID maps all source storages to that storage. Providing the special value '1' will map each source storage to itself. — format `storage-pair-list` |
| `vmid` | number | yes | The (unique) ID of the VM. — format `pve-vmid`, min 100, max 999999999 |
| `with-conntrack-state` | boolean |  | Whether to migrate conntrack entries for running VMs. — default `0` |
| `with-local-disks` | boolean |  | Enable live storage migration for local disk |

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `forceStop` | boolean |  | Make sure the VM stops. — default `0` |
| `keepActive` | boolean |  | Do not deactivate storage volumes. — default `0` |
| `node` | string | yes | The cluster node name. — format `pve-node` |
| `skiplock` | boolean |  | Ignore locks - only root is allowed to use this option. |
| `timeout` | number |  | Wait maximal timeout seconds. — min 0 |
| `vmid` | number | yes | The (unique) ID of the VM. — format `pve-vmid`, min 100, max 999999999 |

### `POST /nodes/{node}/qemu/{vmid}/status/start`

```ts
proxmox.nodes.$(node).qemu.$(vmid).status.start.$post()
```

Start virtual machine.

Returns `string`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `force-cpu` | string |  | Override QEMU's -cpu argument with the given string. |
| `machine` | string |  | Specify the QEMU machine. |
| `migratedfrom` | string |  | The cluster node name. — format `pve-node` |
| `migration_network` | string |  | CIDR of the (sub) network that is used for migration. — format `CIDR` |
| `migration_type` | `secure` \| `insecure` |  | Migration traffic is encrypted using an SSH tunnel by default. On secure, completely private networks this can be disabled to increase performance. |
| `nets-host-mtu` | string |  | Used for migration compat. List of VirtIO network devices and their effective host_mtu setting according to the QEMU object model on the source side of the migration. A value of 0 means that the host_mtu parameter is to be avoided for the corresponding device. |
| `node` | string | yes | The cluster node name. — format `pve-node` |
| `skiplock` | boolean |  | Ignore locks - only root is allowed to use this option. |
| `stateuri` | string |  | Some command save/restore state from this location. — ≤ 128 chars |
| `targetstorage` | string |  | Mapping from source to target storages. Providing only a single storage ID maps all source storages to that storage. Providing the special value '1' will map each source storage to itself. — format `storage-pair-list` |
| `timeout` | number |  | Wait maximal timeout seconds. — min 0, default `"max(30, vm memory in GiB)"` |
| `vmid` | number | yes | The (unique) ID of the VM. — format `pve-vmid`, min 100, max 999999999 |
| `with-conntrack-state` | boolean |  | Whether to migrate conntrack entries for running VMs. — default `0` |

### `POST /nodes/{node}/qemu/{vmid}/status/stop`

```ts
proxmox.nodes.$(node).qemu.$(vmid).status.stop.$post()
```

Stop virtual machine. The qemu process will exit immediately. This is akin to pulling the power plug of a running computer and may damage the VM data.

Returns `string`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keepActive` | boolean |  | Do not deactivate storage volumes. — default `0` |
| `migratedfrom` | string |  | The cluster node name. — format `pve-node` |
| `node` | string | yes | The cluster node name. — format `pve-node` |
| `overrule-shutdown` | boolean |  | Try to abort active 'qmshutdown' tasks before stopping. — default `0` |
| `skiplock` | boolean |  | Ignore locks - only root is allowed to use this option. |
| `timeout` | number |  | Wait maximal timeout seconds. — min 0 |
| `vmid` | number | yes | The (unique) ID of the VM. — format `pve-vmid`, min 100, max 999999999 |

### `PUT /nodes/{node}/qemu/{vmid}/unlink`

```ts
proxmox.nodes.$(node).qemu.$(vmid).unlink.$put()
```

Unlink/delete disk images.

Returns nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `force` | boolean |  | Force physical removal. Without this, we simple remove the disk from the config file and create an additional configuration entry called 'unused[n]', which contains the volume ID. Unlink of unused[n] always cause physical removal. |
| `idlist` | string | yes | A list of disk IDs you want to delete. — format `pve-configid-list` |
| `node` | string | yes | The cluster node name. — format `pve-node` |
| `vmid` | number | yes | The (unique) ID of the VM. — format `pve-vmid`, min 100, max 999999999 |
